name: What should be included in a bathroom remodel contract?

mainEntity.name: What line items should a bathroom remodeling contract include to avoid scope gaps and surprise charges?
mainEntity.text: What line items should a bathroom remodeling contract include to avoid scope gaps and surprise charges?

acceptedAnswer.text: A strong contract protects both the homeowner and the contractor because it defines the exact scope before work starts. It should spell out all major tasks, the specific materials and fixtures, who purchases them, what permit work is included, and how inspections will be handled. It should also clarify demolition debris removal, protection of surrounding areas, waterproofing methods, and what happens if the crew finds rotted framing or old plumbing after demolition. Payment terms should be tied to milestones, not vague promises. The best contracts also include start and finish expectations, warranty terms, and a written change-order process so any additions are priced and approved before work continues. If a contractor is vague about these details, that is usually a warning sign.
acceptedAnswer.description: A bathroom remodel contract should clearly list scope, materials, fixtures, demolition, waterproofing, plumbing, electrical, permits, inspections, timelines, payment schedule, and change-order rules. It should also say what is excluded, who supplies materials, and how hidden damage will be handled.
